reason: The text explicitly describes the people's antagonism toward their leader Moses. The narrative includes: (1) 'וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם־ מֹשֶׁה' - 'the people contended/quarreled with Moses'; (2) 'וַיִּלֶן הָעָם עַל־ מֹשֶׁה' - 'the people murmured/complained against Moses'; (3) accusations that Moses brought them from Egypt to kill them and their families through thirst. The place is subsequently named 'Massa and Meribah' (from ריב - 'quarrel/contend'), commemorating this antagonistic dispute. The people's hostility is unambiguous throughout the passage.
